briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion and xAI Colossus accelerate AGI timelines as US-China compute race intensifies

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models this month, driving record funding and compute buildouts. Geopolitical tensions over AI dominance continue to escalate with new export controls. Prompt injection vulnerabilities persist across deployed systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed Orion-2 achieving new SOTA on multimodal reasoning. Anthropic's Claude 5 and Google's Gemini 3 launched with enhanced agentic capabilities. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 while DeepSeek released a competitive 1T parameter model.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target multi-agent risks while several high-profile jailbreaks surfaced on X.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA shipped 500K H200 GPUs to hyperscalers. Microsoft and Google announced $50B+ data center expansions in Texas and Arizona. TSMC ramped 2nm production dedicated to AI accelerators.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium by 2028?
